pages.title: Energy from reduced fuels
pages.visualReviewer: Codex parent agent (source preparation, not activity review)

concepts.label: Reduced fuels and reduced cofactors
concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

Energy from Reduced Fuels Is Used to Synthesize
ATP in Animals


 ⬣    Carbohydrates, lipids, and amino
      acids are the main reduced fuels
      for the cell.

 ⬣    Electrons from reduced fuels are
      transferred to reduced cofactors
      NADH or FADH2.

 ⬣    Oxidative phosphorylation
      occurs in mitochondria, where
      the energy from NADH and
      FADH2 is used to make ATP.

Figure: Stage 3 electron transfer and oxidative phosphorylation. NADH and FADH2 (reduced electron carriers) supply electrons to the respiratory chain. 2H+ + 1/2 O2 becomes H2O; ADP + Pi becomes ATP.

pages.title: Structure of a mitochondrion
pages.visualReviewer: Codex parent agent (source preparation, not activity review)

concepts.label: Outer and inner membrane permeability
concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025

              Structure of a Mitochondrion


⬣    Outer membrane
            – Relatively porous membrane; allows passage of metabolites

⬣    Inner membrane
            – Relatively impermeable, with proton gradient across it
            – Location of electron transport chain complexes
            – Convolutions called cristae serve to increase the surface area.

⬣    Intermembrane space (IMS)
            - Similar environment to cytosol
            - Higher proton concentration ( lower pH)
⬣    Matrix
            – Location of the citric acid cycle and parts of lipid and amino acid
            metabolism
            – Lower proton concentration (higher pH)

Figure labels: outer membrane freely permeable to small molecules and ions; inner membrane impermeable to most small molecules and ions, including H+. Inner membrane contains respiratory electron carriers (Complexes I–IV), ADP–ATP translocase, ATP synthase (FoF1), other membrane transporters. Cristae, ribosomes, porin channels. Matrix contains pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, citric acid cycle enzymes, fatty acid β-oxidation enzymes, amino acid oxidation enzymes, DNA, ribosomes, many other enzymes, ATP, ADP, Pi, Mg2+, Ca2+, K+, many soluble metabolic intermediates.

pages.title: Universal electron acceptors
pages.visualReviewer: Codex parent agent (source preparation, not activity review)

concepts.label: Nicotinamide hydride transfer
concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
Electrons Are Funneled to Universal Electron Acceptors

              ⬣    Dehydrogenases collect electrons from catabolic pathways and funnel them into
                   universal electron acceptors:

              1- Nicotinamide nucleotides (NAD+ or NADP+)
                     - Catalyze reversible reactions of the general type:
                     reduced substrate + NAD+        ⇄   oxidized substrate + NADH + H+
                     - Two hydrogen atoms are removed from the substrates:
                                One is transferred as a hydride ion (:H-) to NAD(P)+
                                One is released as H+ in the medium

              2- Flavin nucleotides (FMN or FAD)
                      -The oxidized flavin   nucleotide can accept either:
                         One electron (yielding the semiquinone        form) or
                         Two electrons (yielding FADH2 or FMNH2)

pages.title: Electron-carrying molecules
pages.visualReviewer: Codex parent agent (source preparation, not activity review)

concepts.label: Electron, hydrogen atom and hydride transfer
concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
Electrons –              carrying molecules of the Respiratory chain

              ⬣    Oxidative phosphorylation begins with the entry of electrons into the series of electron
                   carriers called the respiratory chain

              ⬣    Three types of electron transfers occur in oxidative phosphorylation:

                           - Direct transfer of electrons
                           -Transfer as a hydrogen atom (H+ + e−)
                           -Transfer as a hydride ion (:H−), which bears two electrons.

              ⬣    The respiratory chain contains five types of electron-carrying molecules

                      -    Nicotinamide nucleotide (NAD+       or NADP+)
                      -    Flavin nucleotide or Flavoproteins      (FMN or FAD)
                      -    Ubiquinone (coenzyme Q or Q)
                      -    Cytochromes
                      -    Iron-sulfur proteins

concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
Standard        Reduction Potentials of Individual Electron Carriers

   Table 19-2 Standard Reduction Potentials of Respiratory Chain and
   Related Electron Carriers
   Redox reaction (half-reaction)                                                   E′° (V)
   2H+ + 2e−→H2                                                                     −0.414
   NAD+  + H+ + 2e−→NADH                                                            −0.320
   NADP+   + H+ + 2e−→NADPH                                                         −0.324
   NADH dehydrogenase (FMN) + 2H+       + 2e−→NADH dehydrogenase (FMNH2)            −0.30
   Ubiquinone + 2H+   + 2e−→ubiquinol                                               0.045
   Cytochrome b   (Fe3+) + e−→cytochrome b (Fe2+)                                   0.077
   Cytochrome c1  (Fe3+) + e−→cytochrome c1    (Fe2+)                               0.22
   Cytochrome c   (Fe3+) + e−→cytochrome c (Fe2+)                                   0.254
   Cytochrome a   (Fe3+) + e−→cytochrome a (Fe2+)                                   0.29
   Cytochrome a3   (Fe3+) + e−→cytochrome a3   (Fe2+)                               0.35
   ½ O2  + 2H+ + 2e−→H2O                                                            0.817

concepts.label: Four complexes and electron routes
concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
Protein Components of the Mitochondrial Respiratory Chain

     ⬣    Four unique electron-carrier complexes catalyze electron transfer through a portion of the chain:

                 -Complex I (from NADH to ubiquinone)
                 -Complex II (from succinate to ubiquinone)
                 -Complex III (from ubiquinone to cytochrome c)
                 -Complex IV (from cytochrome c to O2)

Table 19-3 The Protein Components of the Mitochondrial Respiratory Chain.
| Enzyme complex/protein | Mass (kDa) | Number of subunits | Prosthetic group(s) |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| I NADH dehydrogenase | 850 | 45 (14) | FMN, Fe-S |
| II Succinate dehydrogenase | 140 | 4 | FAD, Fe-S |
| III Ubiquinone: cytochrome c oxidoreductase | 250 | 11 | Hemes, Fe-S |
| Cytochrome c | 13 | 1 | Heme |
| IV Cytochrome oxidase | 204 | 13 (3–4) | Hemes; CuA, CuB |
Parenthetical subunit counts are preserved as printed; this slide does not explain the parentheses.

pages.title: Respiratory chain and proton pumping
pages.visualReviewer: Codex parent agent (source preparation, not activity review)

concepts.label: Proton pumping at complexes I, III and IV
concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
The respiratory chain / Electron transfer chain (ETC)


















                                                         For each pair of electrons transferred
                                                         to O2, 10 protons are pumped out

Figure: intermembrane space (P side) above and matrix (N side) below. NADH + H+ → NAD+ donates 2e− at I; I pumps 4H+. Succinate → fumarate at II; Q/QH2 transfers to III. III pumps 4H+, cytochrome c (2×) transfers electrons to IV, IV pumps 2H+. At IV: 2H+ + 1/2 O2 → H2O. Printed statement says 10 protons pumped out for each pair of electrons transferred to O2; diagram distinguishes the NADH route and succinate entry bypassing I.

concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
Summary of the flow of electrons and protons through
       the four complexes of the respiratory chain.

Figure: NADH + H+ → NAD+ at NADH dehydrogenase (FMN, Fe-S), Complex I. Succinate → fumarate at succinate dehydrogenase (FAD, Fe-S), Complex II. Both feed CoQ/CoQH2. Complex III contains cytochrome b, Fe-S, cytochrome c1 (cytochrome bc1); cytochrome c transfers to Complex IV containing CuA, cytochrome a, CuB–cytochrome a3 (cytochrome a + a3). At IV 1/2 O2 → H2O.

concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
    ATP Synthesis



⬣   The higher negative charge in the matrix attracts the
    protons (H+) back from the intermembrane space to
    the matrix.
⬣   ATP synthase is a membrane-bound F-type ATPase                                          F1
    that contains two functional units Fo       and F1


⬣   ATP synthase allows the reverse movement of most
    of the protons back to the matrix, and uses         the
    energy of the proton gradient to synthesize ATP                                          Fo
    from ADP + Pi.


⬣   Estimated passage of 4 protons (H+) per ATP
    synthesized

pages.visualReviewer: Codex parent agent (source preparation, not activity review)

concepts.label: Inner membrane NADH barrier
concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
               The Malate-Aspartate Shuttle


⬣    The NADH dehydrogenase of the inner
     mitochondrial membrane accepts electrons
     only from NADH in the matrix.

⬣    The inner mitochondrial membrane is not
     permeable to NADH, so Special shuttle
     systems carry reducing equivalents from
     cytosolic NADH.

⬣    The malate-aspartate shuttle is the most
     active NADH shuttle, operating in the
     mitochondria of the liver, kidney, and heart.

⬣    NADH which contributes electrons to Complex
     I of the respiratory chain, leads to the
     production of about 2.5 ATP molecules.

Figure numbered 1–6: cytosolic malate dehydrogenase converts oxaloacetate to malate while NADH + H+ → NAD+ (1); malate–α-ketoglutarate transporter brings malate in and α-ketoglutarate out (2); matrix malate dehydrogenase converts malate to oxaloacetate and NAD+ → NADH + H+ (3); matrix aspartate aminotransferase exchanges oxaloacetate/glutamate with aspartate/α-ketoglutarate (4); glutamate–aspartate transporter exchanges cytosolic glutamate inward and matrix aspartate outward (5); cytosolic aspartate aminotransferase completes the return to oxaloacetate (6). Net effect label: NADH(P side) → NADH(N side). Molecular structures and compartment labels shown.

concepts.label: Glycerol 3-phosphate shuttle tissue and yield
concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
      The Glycerol 3-Phosphate Shuttle


⬣   The glycerol 3-phosphate is an alternative
    shuttle used in skeletal muscle and brain.

⬣   NADH equivalents moved in by a reaction
    catalyzed by cytosolic glycerol 3-phosphate
    dehydrogenase and an isozyme bound to
    the outer face of the inner membrane.


⬣   This shuttle does not involve membrane
    transport systems.


⬣   NADH which contributes electrons to
    Complex III of the respiratory chain, leads to
    the production of about 1.5 ATP molecules.

Figure: glycolysis supplies cytosolic NADH + H+; cytosolic glycerol 3-phosphate dehydrogenase couples NADH → NAD+ to dihydroxyacetone phosphate → glycerol 3-phosphate. Mitochondrial glycerol 3-phosphate dehydrogenase has FAD/FADH2 on outer face of inner membrane; arrow passes via Q → QH2 to Complex III. Intermembrane space (P side), matrix (N side) labelled. Body shorthand says NADH contributes electrons to Complex III; diagram explicitly includes flavin and Q intermediates.

concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
     ATP Yield from Complete Oxidation of Glucose


⬣   Complete oxidation of a molecule of glucose to CO2 yields 30 or 32 ATP

⬣   Glycolysis under anaerobic conditions (lactate fermentation) yields only 2 ATP per glucose

⬣   Oxidative phosphorylation produces most of the ATP made in aerobic cells.

| Acetyl-CoA oxidation in citric acid cycle (two per glucose) | 2 FADH2 | 3 |
| Acetyl-CoA oxidation in citric acid cycle (two per glucose) | 2 ATP or 2 GTP | 2 |
| Total yield per glucose | | 30 or 32 |

pages.title: Regulation by cellular energy needs
pages.visualReviewer: Codex parent agent (source preparation, not activity review)

concepts.label: ADP-dependent acceptor control
concepts.rationale: Explicit midterm mechanism, distinction or relationship.
concepts.detail:
Dr. Osama Essawi 2025
     Oxidative Phosphorylation Is Regulated by Cellular
                                                Energy Needs



⬣    The rate of O₂ consumption in mitochondria is regulated by ADP availability (acceptor control of respiration).

⬣    Cellular energy status is indicated by intracellular ADP concentration and the           [ATP]/[ADP]·[Pi ]  “mass-action
     ratio” (which is typically high  ).

⬣    When energy demand increases (e.g., during protein synthesis), ATP is broken down to ADP + Pi, lowering the
     mass-action ratio.

⬣    Increased ADP availability stimulates oxidative phosphorylation, leading to higher respiration rates and ATP
     regeneration.

⬣    This cycle ensures a stable ATP supply, matching ATP formation to consumption, maintaining cellular energy
     balance.

The visually printed mass-action ratio is [ATP]/[ADP]·[Pi], without enclosing the entire denominator in this slide. Retain the typography; avoid using its ambiguous grouping to score a calculation. Qualitative direction is explicit: ATP consumption raises ADP, stimulates respiration and ATP regeneration.
